tagline: Meeting transcription, summaries, and AI chat over conversations.
verdictSummary: A personal transcription-and-search tool — record or import audio, transcribe locally with speaker labels, summarize with an LLM, search across everything — is a real weekend build. What doesn't come with it is Otter's live meeting-bot behavior, polished multi-speaker diarization, and searchable history synced across devices.
coreLoopDIY: Record or import meeting audio, transcribe it locally with speaker labels, summarize with an LLM, and search across every transcript you've ever saved.
whatYouLose: a bot that joins meetings live
higher-quality speaker diarization on real crosstalk
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for capture reliability and a shared, searchable meeting memory — not just for a transcript file, which is the easy part.
notes: Recognizable but not trivial: a good example of transcription being easy while production-grade capture is not.
prompt:
Build a personal meeting transcription and search tool: a command to capture microphone audio to a file, or import a recording made elsewhere. Transcribe locally with word-level timestamps and speaker diarization, labeling speakers generically and letting you rename them once per meeting. Send the transcript to an LLM for a summary — a short overview, decisions made, action items with owners — saved alongside the full transcript. Build full-text search across every transcript, returning matching lines with the meeting's date and timestamp. Add a simple chat mode: ask a question about a specific meeting and get an answer generated from its transcript.

Do not build a bot that joins Zoom or Meet calls automatically, mobile apps, or team sharing — accept that diarization will be rough on heavy crosstalk, and say so honestly in the README rather than promising more than a local model delivers.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Otter.ai transcripts?
faq.a: Otter lets you export individual transcripts as text, and a short script can bulk-import those into this build's search index — the original audio generally isn't included in the export.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The search and summary views are responsive web pages, usable on a phone to look something up, but there's no dedicated mobile app for capturing meetings on the go.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing extra for local transcription; LLM API usage for summaries and chat costs a small amount per meeting, typically well under a dollar.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Reliable live capture. Otter's bot joins calls and records automatically; here, forgetting to hit record or import a file means that meeting simply isn't in the archive.
